result.text: We're continuing פרק ל"ט and we're talking about how the אותיות are on the one hand they're כלים, on the other hand they're לבושים. And we talked about how when an idea is expressed, for example, it needs to be expressed in אותיות that define it to know that it's that idea and not a different idea. But then there's the aspect of every person is going to express the same idea in their own words or in a different language, and that's like a לבוש, that's a garment, that's something that's external to the essence of the idea and can change. וכך הוא באותיות הרצון, and you have a similar thing with the letters of desire, that our desire is also expressed like we said in אותיות. שהרי רצון אחד פשוט מתלבש בכמה מיני גילויי אופנים שונים, that one, you can have the same essential simple desire and it becomes expressed in many different ways. ואינו רק רצון אחד, and it's just one, it's really just one רצון. Like for example, a person that wants honor or something like that could come out in a lot of different ways, but the you know the essence is the same. וכמו בלבוש יתלבש, or the same thing, a person wants money, a person wants this, right? Or the same thing in spiritual things, a person wants to be close to God, there's a lot of different ways a person could express that. וכמו בלבוש יתלבש הגוף, and just like the body will put on clothing which is, right, a garment that's external to it, כך הרצון בא באופן גלוי שלו להחליף תמיד וכולי. So too the desire becomes expressed in all different types of things, but those external expressions are just a garment to express the essential desire, what the person really wants, right? So a person, whatever it is, if a person wants to like we talk about the metaphor of wanting a house, right, the specifics of, you know, you're going to live there or you're going to live here, it doesn't really matter. It's a different box to put your stuff in, but the essential desire is the same: you want to have a place to feel at home. Again, like we said, a person wants honor or they want to win, so if they play one game it's going to be expressed in this way, it can be another game it's going to be expressed that way, all different types of things like that. Or like back to the idea of the היולי of the חפץ חסד, a person desires kindness, so in one situation they're going to express the kindness by helping a person with this way, with shoes, with coats, with this, with that, whatever it is, with a smile, with a kind word. It's going to come out in many different ways, but the essential desire is the same. וכמו שאנו רואים, like we see, באותיות המחשבה המלבישים למידות, like the letters of thought that are a garment to express a person's emotions, their feelings, שהאהבה שבלב שכבר באה באופן אותיות הגילוי שלה בלב, so when a person has a feeling of love in the heart, so there are certain essential letters that define and make it a feeling of love, and that's the on that level it's a כלי, but then that feeling of love is going to go up to the thought. הנה בבואה במחשבה, when it comes up in thought, הרי היא מתלבשת שם במחשבה זו כגוף שמתלבש בלבוש נפרד ממש. So then the the feeling of love when it comes into the thoughts, it's like a garment which is something separate from it. And שעל זה נאמר, about this it says, כלבוש תחליפם, that it's like a garment that's constantly changed, ממש. שהרי לבוש המחשבה אינו עומד אפילו רגע, like we see that the thought never ceases, it's constantly running. A person's thoughts constantly run with new new words, new thoughts, but they're expressing the same idea. When a person is in love with somebody, they're thinking about them, and they think about it this way and that way, and it's kind of like like the poetry of שיר השירים type of thing, where there's all these different ways of expressing the feeling. And the same thing, you could have the opposite: if a person's angry about something, their mind starts racing, and this said that, he did this, and he said that, and they just keep thinking and thinking about it. Or if a person's worried about something, right, the anxiety will come out in their thoughts running, and they'll think about this and think about that, שתמיד פושט ולובש, פושט ולובש וכולי, is constantly taking off the old garment of the old thought and then putting on a new thought, and taking it off and putting on a new one, ממחשבה למחשבה, from one thought to another thought, וכולי. וכך גם אור השכל בבואו בלבוש דאותיות המחשבה ממש, פושט ולובש ממחשבה למחשבה וכולי. The same thing with the intellect, that the same idea when it comes into letters of thought, the letters of thought become a garment that's constantly changed. And the whole idea is that that anytime something is expressed on its essential level, so an essential רצון or an essential idea or an essential feeling, those have certain אותיות that define them, and those letters are considered כלים. But then when you take something and it's expressed in another level that's external to the essential level, so like the רצון goes into the שכל, or the שכל goes into a מידה, or any of them go go into מחשבה or into דיבור or something like that, then it becomes a לבוש, where it's something that's just a symbol that's expressing it, but it can constantly change. And not only can it change, it's essential that it constantly changes, cuz that's how you express the essential thing. In other words, how do you show that you really, like we talked about back in like פרק א׳, if you want to teach a kid the color red, how do you make sure that they understand the concept? You show them many different examples of the color. You show them a red apple and a red car and a red block, and specifically by showing it in many different contexts, they're able to then recognize and deduce the common denominator, which is the real essential thing that's higher than any of those things. And the same thing with with, you know, expressing a feeling or an idea, because it's expressed in many different ways, that is what allows you to recognize there's really something deeper behind it that's more essential. So that that changing is an important thing. And in a similar way, it talks about elsewhere that the יחידה, to the יחידה, the all of the other כוחות, so the רצון and שכל and מידות and מחשבה, דיבור, מעשה, those are all לבושים that can change. And so that's why like our expression of our connection to God is expressed in the fact that whatever God wants us to do, we'll do. If He tells me to, you know, to keep שבת, I keep שבת. If He tells me to be מחלל שבת to save somebody's life, I'm מחלל שבת. Or if a נביא tells me to go to war on שבת, I go to war on שבת. And, you know, if השם would tell me to chop wood, I'd chop wood. So, the the fact that I'm ready to change from one עבודה to another עבודה, that is what allows me to express that I have an essential connection that's higher than the specifics. So, that's that's the idea. מה שאין כן בבחינת גילוי אותיות השכל בעצם הנ״ל, שנחשבים מהעצם, רק שנראה כמו לבוש לאותיות המחשבה ממש, אחרי שנתהוו במציאות נבדל מן העצם השכל וכולי כנ״ל. In contrast, the letters of the שכל itself when that's actually defining the idea, that's considered part of the essence. It's just that it appears like a לבוש like the letters of מחשבה once those letters are created, and then they become something that's separate from the עצם השכל, then they In other words, when you take anytime you take an idea, you have to put it when you put it into words, you have to put it into words of let's say a language, you put it in Hebrew, in Yiddish, into English, then that external aspect of the letters is like a לבוש that you could express in a different way. But there is a certain essential idea of those אותיות that you need to have to define the idea, and that's considered the כלי. ונמצא מובן, so it comes out understood from here, דשניהם אמת, that they're both true, that that אותיות are both כלים and they are לבושים. בשרש בחינת האותיות, about the root of letters, דלפעמים הם בבחינת כלים, sometimes they are כלים, they're a vessel, which is like an essential and integral, inherent to the thing, בהיותם בשרש מחצבתם באחדות גמור עם העצם כנ״ל, when they're in their root, in their source, where they're one with the essence, וגם הם נעשים בבחינת לבושים נפרדים, and they also become these external לבושים, these garments that are just manifesting the idea, that are separate from נפרדים מן העצם לגמרי, they're completely separate from the essence כנ״ל, and therefore they can change. להיות כי שורש האותיות מבחינת מקיפים, and this is because the source of the letters are from the מקיפים, the idea of like סובב כל עלמין or the letter the light that's that transcends a particular expression, שהן שורש הלבושים, that that is the source of the garments, ומשם גם כן שורש הכלים המגבילים ומציירים, but that's also the source of the כלים that limit and define things, כנ״ל, like we explained before about how from the thickening of the light comes the כלים, וכמו שמבואר במקום אחר, and as is explained elsewhere. ובכל זה יובן למשכיל למעלה דרך כלל בכל בחינת לבושים דמחשבה דיבור ומעשה, and from this, from this explanation of the relationship of the letters to the light, somebody that is going to try to understand Godliness can recognize the נמשל of the idea of the three לבושים of מחשבה, דיבור, מעשה, ג׳ מיני אותיות, these are three types of letters, בכל פרטי עשר ספירות דהשתלשלות, and these exist on every single level of the סדר השתלשלות. There's מחשבה, דיבור, מעשה in the עצמות אור אין סוף before the צמצום, and then in אדם קדמון, the רצון קדום, אדם קדמון, אצילות, בריאה, יצירה ועשיה, on every level you have these different types of letters, like we're going to also talk more about in coming chapters. But the what this essential idea of recognizing how these letters can be both כלים and לבושים is something that we can understand from here. עד רום המעלות, all the way to the highest levels, בעצמות אור אין סוף, באותיות דגלגלתא ודיקנא בטהירו עילאה, all the way to the essential essential light of the infinite light, in the letters that were engraved there, in the upper, in the upper light or the upper purity. So I always used to translate טהירו עילאה as the upper purity, but I think another translation of טהירו is light, and I think that maybe is the more accurate translation: the upper light. וכאי גוונא ודי למבין, and that is sufficient to understand. So, I think the משל is pretty clear, and then just to think a little bit about some aspects of how this relates to other things. So one idea is in תורה ומצוות, this is something we touched upon earlier, that there's two aspects of the תורה ומצוות. There's part of it that's the essential thing, and then there's part of it that is like a לבוש. So for example, in every הלכה, when משה was shown the תורה on הר סיני, he was told מ״ט פנים לטהר ומ״ט פנים לטמא, 49 reasons to say that it's כשר, or טהור, 49 reasons to say that it's not okay, or it's טמא. And אלו ואלו דברי אלקים חיים. If you look in the תלמוד, and ראשונים and אחרונים, there's many different opinions. And we say like בית שמאי, בית הלל, they could be, that Judaism would be extremely different if you followed בית שמאי instead of בית הלל on many, many things. And there's all different types of opinions, but they're all considered part of the תורה. In other words, there as far as the essence of the תורה, it could be expressed in these different ways. But then there's an idea that once a certain way is פסק'נד as the הלכה, then we have to follow that way. And the same thing we have in a similar way like מנהגים, different people do different things, there's different רבנים. And so we have to be able to recognize that the real essence of the תורה is the fact that I'm ready to do what God wants and be committed to Godliness, make that my priority. And that could be expressed in many different ways and they're valid. And then another part of the תורה is that once we choose a certain path, we're able to commit to that path even though other path that paths exist. And having the ביטול to be able to say, like it says in the פסוק, the מצוה to listen בכל אשר יורוך, to whatever, whichever way they פסקן, אפילו, you know, ימין ושמאל, even if you feel like the right should be left and left should be right and you feel that's like should be the opposite, you have to be able to have that deference and say, okay, we're going to do it this way. And once, and so once you plug that ביטול in, then that becomes an essential, Godly expression. The fact that I'm doing it specifically this way because the תורה said so, listening to the פסק, the way it's in שולחן ערוך and the רבנים and things like that. But then there's a stage where like a רב or something is debating, and it could go either way and they're both valid. And they have to, you know, look at it. And then there's also certain things where we have to be ready to be flexible. And let's say, these days we don't do it so much, but there used to be a concept of מנהג המקום. If you go to a certain place, you do it the way they do it in that place. And have that itself, that you can recognize that this way is okay and my way, you know, my way and their way, they're both fine as long as it's לשם שמים, and so I'm ready to do the מנהג המקום and show respect for that, that that ביטול is what allows the essence to plug in to something that that is external. And in general, these two sides are like the פנימיות התורה and the revealed parts of תורה. That the פנימיות התורה is bringing out the real essence and the spirit of the law, which is the כלי of it, where it's really essentially a Godly thing, and the external way that it's expressed is like a לבוש. And that can be different for all different people in different times, different places. But again, once you plug into it, it takes on that quality of the עצם if it's done with the right perspective. And that's the idea of doing תורה ומצוות with ביטול and having שמחה של מצוה and certain things that make the מצוה that we're doing not just an external action, but makes it a Godly thing. So that's one aspect of it. Another aspect of this idea of the אותיות... Yeah. Right. So there's this big question in things in life: Should I be decisive, or should I be flexible? And so the idea is that and we're going to talk more about this when we talk about תוהו and תיקון, and so what we also we talked about it previously with תוהו and תיקון, I guess, that you we need to have the ביטול to be flexible, and there's a certain stage when that's important. I'll tell you a simple thing that I think really answers your question is that I heard from numerous people that the רבי, when he was deciding to do something new, would spend a lot of time deliberating before he decided to do it, but once he committed to do it and made a decision, he wouldn't change his mind. And so, I think that's the idea is like we need to be able to be careful and flexible and see both sides, like when there's a debate about a הלכה between the רבנים, or when a question comes up to a רב and they have to פסקן, it's very important to see all the sides and consider them all and see the merits of all of them, and recognize that any of them could be okay. And like again, as like like a parent or a teacher, a lot of times when kids will ask, "Can we do this?" or something like that, I, from my perspective, from a more mature perspective, I can look at it and say, "Well, it doesn't really matter if we do it or don't do it or if we do it this way or do it that way. It's not essential." And so then there's different considerations how to make that decision. But what is essential is that once we make a decision, once we commit to doing something in a certain way, we're able to have the the commitment and the ביטול to follow through and and and not like once we agreed to this, could be certain rules or a certain system, you have to be very very reticent, it's very careful before you start changing or compromising on that, because otherwise your like it the the idea of of מלכות, of having like firm limits that are outside of your control, are called the כוס של ברכה, that's the cup that holds blessings. And you see that like in anything in life, that our ability to be successful requires that we first have a certain discipline. So like if a person wants to learn like to learn a language, first you have to have the discipline to learn the vocabulary and learn to speak properly and clearly, and then you have the freedom to express yourself. When you're learning to write, you have to learn spelling and grammar and all that kind of stuff, and first it just requires effort to learn learn how to read and learn how to write, but once you master it, then you have freedom of expression. The same thing if you want to learn how to play an instrument, you have to first have that discipline to go through the practice and study it and do your scales, but then you that becomes a כלי for freedom of expression. So the same thing with a lot of things in תורה ומצוות, like there's a היום יום from, I think it's כ״ה שבט actually, about how the laws of the תורה create life, human laws that man make are created by life. But תורה creates life, and I think a big part of that is that, yes, society changes and times change, and in certain ways the תורה and הלכה and מנהגים have changed based on that, but in general, it doesn't really matter like the rules that we, a lot of these things, the way we decide to do things, it's kind of like the rules of a game. It could go, it doesn't really matter how you do it. Whatever system you're in, no system, like רמב״ם talks about this in מורה נבוכים, no system is going to be perfect. But on the other hand, I can thrive within any system if I'm willing to have the ביטול to learn it and master it and be flexible, and it's more important for me, in most situations it's more important for me to learn to be flexible, and me to learn to work within a system and read and and be compelled to reach in and develop my talents and abilities, than to just change the system to make it easier for me and be lazy. And that's, you know, and I think that's a really important thing, the תורה is trying to create a situation that's compelling us to reach into ourselves and be able to go against the currents of our society and be a godly person that's that's a creative contributor and has this inner sense of a moral compass and what's right and wrong and I'm trying to bring that out to the world. And so the framework of the תורה ומצוות gives me the the fact that I'm not going to change that creates a structure that forces me to to go inside to change and therefore gives me the power to really change myself and change the world around me. If a person will just have like a false sense of kindness and want to just be lenient on themselves or on a child and say, "Oh, we'll just change the rules for them," like is happening a lot in our society today, it actually is detrimental because then it prevents the person from developing the skills they need to really develop their potential and really, you know, be be productive and really be a creative contributor and stuff like that. So that's kind of the yeah, the nature of these things that, on the one hand, we have to recognize that there these are external things that can change and it could come in many ways and have that flexibility, but once we plug into them, they they become like a כלי that's essential. So, you know, yeah, it's so to just to recap, to answer your question, generally, before doing something, you need to be flexible In your thinking and be ready to take any approach and consider any option. Once you commit to something, you have to be very careful before changing it, because you have to make sure it's not coming from laziness. In other words, if a person really can't do something, like if a kid really can't do something, then you should make an exception for them. If a person really needs a היתר, a good רב is going to give them a היתר, but you know, you have to really be careful that you're not robbing them of the pressure they need to to be, you know, to be successful, be excellent. And sometimes that's a positive pressure, even if at first it's a little bit of a גבורה. So that's the, you know, the challenge with these things. Right. Right. Yeah, like you're saying, if a person is too committed to their business, they don't even make time to spend with their kids, then, yeah, they maybe have to rethink their priorities and adjust things. And that's the idea that every now and then we have to have a חשבון הנפש or we have to have a משפיע or a רב or something that we go to and get advice and, you know, and think about these things. And, but again, it's something that we we can't The problem is that we can't do that every day all the time, because if we're always second-guessing our choices, then we can't act. So we have to have certain times, that's the idea of like ראש השנה, and or on a birthday, or once a week on Thursday night, there are certain times to make a חשבון הנפש and reconsider our priorities and our choices and our direction in life. But most of the time we have to be committed to doing, to action, because that's the only thing that's going to get things done, even if sometimes it's better to take action even if it's not perfect than to spend never do anything because we're spending too much time worrying about if it's going to be right. So that's that's part of the balance there. And then another aspect of the נמשל with these things is that it says that souls, נשמות, are come from the אותיות of מחשבה, and מלאכים come from the אותיות of דיבור. And so in a נשמה, we also have these two sides, that part of the נשמה is a חלק אלוקה, which is an essential thing, it's it's one with God, and it's comes from pure אלוקות. But then each person gets their personality and a unique character, which is an external thing, which are like a לבוש. And that can change. And in general, every person is made up of these three parts: we have our essence that doesn't change, then we have our כוחות, which are like the כלים for us, which is our the the the שכל and מידות, and those can change, but they don't totally We can develop them, they don't totally change. And then we have our לבושים of מחשבה דיבור ומעשה, which can change completely. But then some from a higher perspective, even the כוחות are like a לבוש to the עצם הנפש. And so we have this idea that on every level, what might be essential on one level is a לבוש compared to a higher level. And so that's the basic idea that we have to understand and recognize. And a similar thing with the ספירות, that the ספירות on a certain level are essential, but on a certain level they're like a לבוש, because God could have chosen other ספירות, it didn't have to be these ספירות, God could have chosen things that aren't ספירות. And also within each ספירה, the fact that God chooses to make create the world and have תרי״ג מצוות with that certain things make sense and logical, that logic and reason is something that God is creating, and it's like a לבוש. God could have made other things make sense, and that would have made sense to us. So recognizing that God is setting up the system and creating the system, but then once He creates it, He plugs His essence into it, and then it becomes essential, like, you know, it's true that gravity could have worked differently if God wanted it to, but it doesn't, and so we have to we're living in this reality. So those are the two sides of seeing it: seeing on the one hand that God is higher than these things, and on the other hand at a certain level they become essential. So that's the basic idea on all these levels of סדר השתלשלות. And a lot of these ideas, once we learn them, we also have to go think back and revise our understanding of all the previous levels, like when we talked about the רצון קדום and the ספירות of עיגולים going into יושר, that's the similar process of the essence. So the עיגולים are like the essence and that's like the כלים, and then when they come into יושר that's like a לבוש for it. And the same thing with in אצילות and everything like that.
